verdicts.reason: Critique handling: both share the loss-conditioned same-length revision, but X also keeps the verifier's family out of the final panel, adds an ambition guard and a reason filter, and sets explicit kill thresholds, whereas Y lists the shared-family failure mode and leaves it unaddressed.

Evidence and testability: both share the expected-maximum portfolio rule, but X fits tau from saved-run residuals leave-one-brief-out, gates on label kappa and minimum comparisons, and pre-registers kill criteria, whereas Y hard-codes tau at 0.5 SD with no stopping rule.

Testability with the benchmark: X tests on 10 briefs with a primary blinded comparison against the single agent's top 3 and explicit kill thresholds including an ambition guard, whereas Y's one-brief test cannot establish preference over the baseline.

Testability and fit to brief: X runs 10 briefs against a matched-token prose-feedback control with win rate versus the single agent as primary, plus kill criteria, whereas Y tests one brief using only falsified-claim rate and never measures rater preference.
Mechanism soundness: X re-ranks finals on fresh comparisons to avoid winner's-curse selection from the in-loop judge and adds a kill criterion; Y is otherwise identical and has neither.

Critique handling: X fits on one panel and scores on a different-family panel, which honours its own Goodhart assumption and has a kill rule, whereas Y's test labels with the evaluation panel and so contradicts that assumption.

Testability: X's offline test crosses weighting with allocation at equal votes, caps each judge's share and pre-registers a tau-gain kill rule, whereas Y compares only uniform against judge-aware weighting with no stopping criterion.

Statistical validity of the test: X analyses child-beats-parent paired by brief because contests within a brief are correlated, and it centres the prior on the global rate, whereas Y's per-contest power calculation overstates power.

Critique handling and fit to brief: X adds a two-family 4/4 gate and a paraphrase placebo that measures style bias, and it takes the benchmark win rate against the single agent as primary outcome, whereas Y has one verifier that may share the panel's family and measures only revised versus original.

Mechanism soundness: X fits tau from rating correlation, caps any mean-of-3 loss and reduces exactly to top-3 when finalists are diverse, so it costs nothing on a null, and it tests win rate against the single agent; Y fixes tau arbitrarily and has no such safeguards.

Fit to brief: X's codebase probes make this brief's qualitative 'implementable in this codebase' claims checkable, poorly checkable cards fall back to median rather than last place, and a step-0 check on checkable fraction can kill the idea, whereas Y leaves qualitative briefs undiscriminated and penalised.

Implementability and testability: X runs on its own with its own extractor, caps tokens at 1.4x, reverts over-struck cards and measures win rate against the single agent with kill criteria, whereas Y depends on another card's ledger and tests one brief without a preference outcome.

Critique handling: X accepts variants under a gate family outside both the ranker and the benchmark panel, measures the overfit gap against a held-out family and sets kill thresholds, whereas Y's acceptance judge can be overfit by the mutants.

Mechanism soundness: X uses a within-run conditional logit to cancel brief effects, stages learning with sign-constrained nuisance weights usable at about 5 briefs, uses non-panel labellers and kills on oracle headroom, whereas Y needs 15 briefs and its test labels with the evaluation panel.

Evidence and testability: X calibrates position, self-preference and a shared verbosity term without labels using probes, shrinks a_j so only it needs about 100 external votes, and stages the test with a kill rule, whereas Y needs about 300 externally rated votes and ignores verbosity.

Implementability and testability: X defines its own contest gate, warm-starts offline from saved finalists and has a stage-1 chi-square kill test on whether operators differ at all, whereas Y depends on card 0's loop and rests on a power calculation that ignores clustering within briefs.
